tiers.block: Do not ship. Accessibility, honesty and basic correctness. Fix it or record why it does not apply.
tiers.tell: A common default that makes a page read as machine-made. Replace it with a deliberate choice, or record why it is deliberate here.
tiers.note: Worth a look. A pattern that is often a symptom, not a fault.

rules.title: No viewport meta tag
rules.why: Phones render the desktop layout shrunk down.
rules.fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">.

rules.title: No lang attribute on <html>
rules.why: Screen readers and translation tools guess the language.
rules.fix: Add lang="en-GB" or the right code.

rules.title: Image without alt text
rules.why: Content is invisible to screen readers; decorative images need alt="".
rules.fix: Describe the image, or use alt="" if it is decoration.

rules.title: Focus outline removed with no replacement
rules.why: Keyboard users lose track of where they are.
rules.fix: Style :focus-visible with a clear ring instead of removing the outline.

rules.title: Animation with no prefers-reduced-motion handling
rules.why: Motion can cause real discomfort for some people.
rules.fix: Wrap motion in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) or switch it off in the reduce case.

rules.title: Placeholder copy left in
rules.why: Lorem ipsum or template text means the page is not finished.
rules.fix: Write the real copy, or leave the section out.

rules.title: Statistics or claims with no source
rules.why: Figures such as '10k+ users' or '99.9% uptime' are invented unless you can point to where they come from.
rules.fix: Use a figure you can source and cite it, or describe what the thing does instead.

rules.title: An override with no reason
rules.why: An ignore comment must say why, or it is just hiding the problem.
rules.fix: Write: anti-slop-ignore <rule-id>: <reason>.

rules.title: Purple or indigo gradient
rules.why: The single most common default colour treatment from language models.
rules.fix: Choose a colour from the subject (a material, a place, a brand, a print tradition) and use it flat.

rules.title: Gradient-filled headline text
rules.why: Clipped gradient text is a reflex used to make a heading feel designed.
rules.fix: Set the heading in one colour and get emphasis from size, weight or position.

rules.title: Default typeface as the main face
rules.why: Inter, Roboto, Poppins or the bare system stack signals that no typographic choice was made.
rules.fix: Pick a face for a reason and pair it with a contrasting one; see references/typography.md.

rules.title: Frosted glass panels
rules.why: Blurred translucent cards are a trend default that hurts contrast.
rules.fix: Use a solid surface and a border, and keep the glass for places where seeing through helps.

rules.title: Large radius on everything
rules.why: Uniform rounded-2xl corners make every element the same soft shape.
rules.fix: Choose one radius scale, keep most things sharper, and round only what should feel touchable.

rules.title: Heavy shadows on many elements
rules.why: Large soft shadows everywhere flatten hierarchy into a pile of floating cards.
rules.fix: Use borders and spacing for grouping, and a shadow only for things that truly float.

rules.title: Scale-up on hover as the hover effect
rules.why: A hover:scale-105 on every card is a stock interaction.
rules.fix: Change what matters (underline, colour, offset, reveal) and keep layout still.

rules.title: Emoji used as icons
rules.why: Emoji in headings, buttons and feature lists read as filler and render differently on every platform.
rules.fix: Use a consistent icon set, or no icons.

rules.title: Small uppercase label above every heading
rules.why: The tracked-out eyebrow is repeated on every section by habit.
rules.fix: Keep one at most, and only where it carries information.

rules.title: Announcement pill above the headline
rules.why: 'New', 'Now in beta' and sparkle pills are a template opener.
rules.fix: Cut it, or say something specific and dated in the headline itself.

rules.title: Stock marketing vocabulary
rules.why: Words such as seamless, elevate, unlock and supercharge carry no information.
rules.fix: Say what the product does, to whom, in plain words.

rules.title: Long dashes through the copy
rules.why: Several em or en dashes in page text is a recognisable machine habit.
rules.fix: Use full stops, commas, colons or brackets.

rules.title: Default Tailwind indigo, violet or purple
rules.why: The framework's stock accent colours appear on a huge share of generated pages.
rules.fix: Define your own palette as variables and name the colours for what they are for.

rules.title: Blurred glowing blobs in the background
rules.why: Large blurred circles are a decorative reflex with no meaning.
rules.fix: Use real imagery, a pattern with a purpose, or plain space.

rules.title: Stock person names
rules.why: Names such as Sarah Chen or John Doe are the first ones a model reaches for.
rules.fix: Use real, permitted names, or remove the person.

rules.title: Testimonial section
rules.why: A row of quotes with names and job titles is almost always invented in generated pages.
rules.fix: Keep it only if the quotes are real and you have permission, and link to the source.

rules.title: Three identical cards in a row
rules.why: Icon, heading and sentence in three equal columns is the default way to list features.
rules.fix: Vary the scale and the order, or write it as prose or a table.

rules.title: Almost everything centred
rules.why: Centring every block removes the reading edge and any sense of structure.
rules.fix: Set body text left aligned on a clear column, and centre only short, single lines.

rules.title: Generic button labels
rules.why: 'Get started' and 'Learn more' say nothing about what happens next.
rules.fix: Name the action: 'Download the checklist', 'Book a 20 minute call'.

rules.title: No <main> landmark
rules.why: Assistive technology uses landmarks to jump to the content.
rules.fix: Wrap the primary content in <main>.

rules.title: Not exactly one <h1>
rules.why: A page needs one top-level heading that says what it is.
rules.fix: Use one <h1> and keep the rest in order.
